english.title: Cause the falsification of a document / documents relevant to a complex / serious fraud investigation
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowing or suspecting that an investigation by the

(A)_[police]_
(B)_[Serious Fraud Office]_

into a serious or complex fraud was being or was likely to be carried out, caused another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), to falsify, conceal, destroy or otherwise dispose of

(C)_[a document, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DOCUMENT..),]_
(d)_[documents, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DOCUMENTS..),]_

which you knew or suspected were or would be relevant to such an investigation
english.legislation: Contrary to section 2(16) and (17) of the Criminal Justice Act 1987.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing / suspecting that an investigation by the police / Serious Fraud Office
into a serious / complex fraud was being / was likely to be carried out
caused another to falsify / conceal / destroy / otherwise dispose of a document / documents
which you knew / suspected were / would be relevant to such an investigation

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 2(16) of the Criminal Justice Act 1987 provides that the suspect shall be guilty of an offence unless they prove that they had no intention of concealing the facts disclosed by the documents from persons carrying out such an investigation.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
